@@40399089 <h> Sinking Greek village highlights nation 's addiction to coal <p> PTOLEMAIDA , Greece ( AP ) -- If earthquakes struck in slow motion , the results might be visible in a place like the Greek village of Anargyri , a hardscrabble enclave in a black landscape gutted by coal mining . <p> The village in northern Greece once had more than 400 people . Now it has fewer than 50 , after being torn apart over decades . Its roads are slowly buckling , its door frames have shifted , its walls and home foundations have cracked beyond repair . Residents are leaving not in panic but out of desperation . <p> One after another , the tiny villages in Greece 's lignite belt have been destroyed by mining as the ground becomes too unsteady to hold homes upright . Bells at one church in the area are not rung regularly for fear of causing more cracks in the walls . <p> Cattle farmer Michalis Bitas first noticed the damage to homes in Anargyri in 1986 . <p> " That 's when mining started locally . It slowly began to eat up the houses before it went on @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ <p> Bitas is from one of the few dozen households in the village who have refused a power company 's offer to move them to a rented apartment in a nearby town . These villagers are demanding full compensation for their homes -- a right only granted by law if mining occurs directly below a settlement . <p> " I have sheep and machinery . What am I supposed to do ? Move them into an apartment ? " Bitas said . <p> Heavy-duty coal excavators and vehicles on the horizon near the village look like toy trucks , dwarfed by the scale of the blackened mining fields . <p> Greek is still hooked on coal , despite warnings about the dire consequences of global warming issued both by a new scientific report and experts at the recent U.N . climate talks in Poland and despite ambitious European Union-wide targets to replace coal use with renewable energy . <p> Greece is currently the world 's 12th largest producer of lignite -- known as brown coal -- mining 36 million tons annually , according to U.S. federal government energy data . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ dioxide emissions than black coal . It is often burned near where it is mined since its low energy density makes it too expensive to transport very far . <p> Nearly a third of Greece 's electricity is produced by coal-fired plants and the country has no phase-out plan to stop using domestically produced coal , unlike most parts of Western Europe . Despite abundant wind and sun , only around 15 percent of Greece 's energy is produced by renewable sources . Most of its reduction in coal use in recent years has been offset by an increased use of imported natural gas . <p> Under measures hammered out with Greece 's bailout creditors , the state-controlled power company , PPC , will privatize three coal-fired electricity plants , prolonging their life . <p> Also , contrary to many of its EU neighbors , Greece is on course to expand its dependence on oil and gas as the nation tries to attract overseas investment to counter a financial crisis that lasted nearly a decade . The Greek government has embarked on a major exploration drive for oil and gas @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and gas ventures have alarmed environmental groups , which have issued an urgent plea to the Greek government to reverse its course and switch investments to the renewable sources like solar and wind power . <p> " We must act directly to reduce greenhouse gas emissions , but our country is moving in the opposite direction , " a letter addressed to Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras said . It was signed by 34 environmental and human rights groups , including Greenpeace , the World Wide Fund for Nature , Amnesty International and Doctors Without Borders . <p> Greece is planning to invest " in fossil fuels for decades , along with worrying delivery of hundreds of thousands of square kilometers , on and offshore , for hydrocarbon extraction , " the letter said . " This would surrender the country to the nightmare consequences of climate change . " <p> In Anargyri , despite the destruction of their homes , residents have mixed feelings about coal , since PPC is a key employer that provides 5,000 local jobs . The other attraction is that lignite , mined domestically , is @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ unlike imported oil and gas , which in Greece mostly comes from Russia . <p> " Clearly , lignite activity will be reduced and will be replaced by other sources of energy , renewable sources of energy , " PPC executive Konstantinos Theodoridis told The Associated Press . <p> " But lignite will continue to be a strategic fuel that , in any geopolitical instability , is the only energy-producing fuel that is absolutely controlled by our country , " he said .

@@40406589 <h> Rethinking Agro-Tourism In Nigeria <p> For long , people had been traveling to places outside their own homes and staying there for a while for leisure , business , or relaxation . That is simply what tourism is all about . <p> According to World Tourism Organisation ( UNWTO ) , " Tourism comprises the activities of persons traveling to and staying in places outside their usual environment for not more than one consecutive year for leisure , business and other purposes . " <p> There are different types of tourism based on the type of activity , location or duration of stay . Thus , you have such things such as cultural tourism , heritage tourism , geo-tourism , historical tourism etc . <p> What is then agro-tourism ? Agro-tourism in like manner can be described as all activities of farmers aimed at attracting , accommodating and entertaining tourists in an agricultural and rural setting for a fee . <p> Potentials <p> It has been long since Agro-tourism was discovered to have the potential of creating fabulous wealth for farmers . <p> A study conducted in 2004 by Agri Tourism Development Corporation ( ATDC ) , showed @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ left in the villages . It also found that 97% of urban population wants to experience the rustic beauty of the village life . That shows that in agricultural activities there is a rewarding opportunity to develop agro-tourism centre in the villages . <p> Having recognised that farmer 's incomes are seasonal because of the seasonal nature of farming , while their expenses were regular , Shri Pandurang Taware , sought to find a way of making farming sustainable . After three years of research , he discovered that there was need for agro-tourism to generate incomes all year round to compensate for the regular expenses of farmers . Consequently , Taware in 2005 in Malegaon near Baramati in Maharashtra embarked on Agriculture Development Trust 's farm with a two-year project , which become very successful . <p> Thus in 2007 , the ATDC launched Maharashtra State Agri Tourism Vistar Yojana 2007 in which he selected 52 farmers to pioneer the Agri-tourism centres across the state of Maharashtra . In 2008 , he also recruited another set of 25 farmers making it 72 Agro-tourism centres currently operational in the state @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ under co-operative basis , the farmers started several agro-tourism development co-operatives in the area and they were successful . <p> The Songhai Farms in Porto-Novo , Republic of Benin is run on a similar principle of agro-tourism . <p> Songhai operates a kind of integrated farming system with sections for plant production , animal production , fish farming , all linked together in the primary production system with each being complementary to the other . <p> There is no waste there as the residues from after harvests and food processing are reinvested for further production . <p> There structure has other ancillary facilities for restaurants where organic food produced in the farms are served , hotel accommodation for visitors , swimming pool , chapel , conference and communication facilities , cars for hire , among other services they provide for tourists . <p> How It Works <p> The idea can be replicated here . One or a group of farmers can join hands to establish agro-tourism centres where they can embark on large scale poultry , fish farming , piggery , grass cutter and rabbit farming , fruit and vegetable @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <p> There should be provision of facilities for hotel/lodging , recreational facilities such as field for games , swimming pool , children 's play centres as well as training facilities . <p> An agro-tourist centre offers visitors opportunity to try other things such as riding horses , tasting pure honey , savouring local dishes , picking fresh fruits and vegetables , visiting stands for local and regional produce and shopping in hand-craft gift items shops . Students of colleges and universities can take time off to visit to try out organic farming in a rural setting . They can as well share thoughts and experiences with farmers on indigenous farming methods , share indigenous farmers ' experiences on a number of issues such as climate change , global warming , crisis relating to ground water and arsenic pollutions , bio-fertilizers , among others . <p> Agro-Tourism Centres In Nigeria <p> There are some semblances of Songhai model of agro-tourism in Nigeria . We have some state initiatives such as in Abi , Cross River State , Abudu Cattle Ranch in Calabar , Avia in Lagos , Meruwa and Makera @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Enugu , Okomu Oil Palm Plantation in Benin , Nigeria , to mention but a few . However , they are not many and not as developed as the Songhai Farms of the Republic of Benin . <p> Farmers and those interested in farming should maximise the full potentials of agro-tourism such as growing multiple streams of income . It is reminiscent of Farm Settlements of old . It is a veritable means of opening up and developing rural areas , promoting entrepreneurship and sills acquisition in rural areas as well as stemming migration of youths from rural areas to city centres in search of few or non-existent jobs . <p> Corporate entities and farmers ' cooperatives should be interested in the development of agro-tourism in the country for it is one of the fastest ways to empower jobless youths , create sustainable wealth for farmers , ensure food security and improve health of the citizens . This has the ripple effect of diversifying the economy through agriculture . <p> The Federal and state governments and wealthy individuals should promote agro-tourism centres all over the country as a way of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of their entrepreneurial skills and training in various aspects of agriculture . Above all , remember that one can start small and grow into a conglomerate . So do not be afraid to take action .

@@40413192 <h> China , UK develop cold storage rail container <p> Experts from University of Birmingham and CRRC Shijiazhuang of China have developed the world 's first shipping container using materials that store and release cold energy . <p> CRRC Shijiazhuang is one of one of China 's biggest railway rolling stock companies . <p> Using phase change material ( PCM ) , Birmingham scientists and their counterparts at CRRC Shijiazhuang , have developed a ' refrigerated ' truck-to-train container that is easier and more efficient to operate than conventional equipment . <p> Once ' charged ' , PCM inside the container -- which can be transferred from train to truck and vice versa -- can keep the inside temperature between 5-12 ? C for up to 120 hours . <p> The technology has recently completed commercial trials carrying real goods for 35,000 kilometres of road and 1000 kilometres of rail transport across different climate zones . <p> Professor Yulong Ding , Director of Birmingham Energy Storage Centre , who led the research at Birmingham , said : " Energy storage is an area of world-leading expertise at the University of Birmingham and cold chain technologies research is one of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <p> " We have developed a productive collaboration with CRRC Shijiazhuang and this innovative technology marks the beginning of developing an efficient and economic rail &amp; road freight cold chain . <p> " We are proud to contribute to the development of safe and clean low carbon energy technologies in China and beyond , which will ultimately help us to reduce the energy burden on our planet and tackle climate change . " <p> Cooling is essential to modern society , which already causes twice the global greenhouse emissions of shipping and aviation combined with the cold chain being a significant cause of pollution . All tribes love money and that 's where the problem lies , " Aliu adds . <p> That has never come in the way of the cordial relationship between farmers and herders , he says , reaffirming that " the two @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ anything threaten the peace we enjoy . " Echoing those sentiments is Alhaji Yakubu Bello , the Oyo State Chairman of Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association and the Seriki Fulani , Ibarapa areas . <p> " We settle our matters amicably even without the police , " says Bello . " But the Miyetti Allah holds a regular meeting which it has also turned into a ' school ' where herders are educated on the ' dos and don'ts ' ( in dealing with farmers ) because we do n't want problem , " the Miyetti Allah leader explains . <p> One of the traditional rulers Bello refers to as the arbiters is the Sobaloju of Eruwaland , Chief Afolabi Opatoyinbo @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ least a day of the week to entertaining farmers-herdsmen issues at the palace of the town 's monarch , the Eleruwa of Eruwa . <p> Part of their terms of reference is to hear complaints , inspect damages , summon the perpetrator and charge the person according to the size of the loss . In keeping the peace between farmers and herders , Opatoyinbo says an unlikely factor uniting the two distinct communities is intermarriage . <p> " Intermarriages happen and our people also keep livestock with Fulani , to demonstrate our cordial relationship with . Excess Crude Account is a special account established to warehouse excess revenues from the prevailing crude oil price at the international market . Income generated above the approved crude oil benchmark price in the annual budget is saved in the account . Withdrawal from the account is subject to the approval of the three tiers of government and the Executive Council of the Federation ( FEC ) . It was not clear when the decision to draw from the account was taken and for what purpose . <h> Skewed appointments <p> Controversies also trailed Buhari 's appointments since 2015 , when he mounted the saddle as president . While proceedings have been suspended , the appeal would travel for many years up to the Supreme Court , which would then , in most cases , dismiss the appeal and ask the defendants to go back to the trial court for the case to be re-opened . <p> However , the passage of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015 by former President Goodluck Jonathan marked the dawn of a new era in the Nigerian criminal justice @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , abolished stay of proceedings . <p> Another interesting provisions of the Act is Section 396(3) and ( 4 ) which stipulated that " hearings shall be on a daily basis , but in exceptional cases , while adjournments , not to be in excess of 14 working days , may be granted , but such adjournments must not exceed five in any proceedings . <p> But it is not yet Uhuru as defence lawyers have started to deploy other tricks , which were not envisaged by the ACJA , to delay criminal cases and keep them perpetually in court . <p> Among such new dilatory tricks are long cross-examination of witnesses by defence lawyers ; intimidation of judges through petitions and complaints of alleged bias ; filing of no-case submission and constant resort to appeal as exemplified by the ongoing N400million alleged fraud case of a former Publicity Secretary of the Peoples Democratic Party , Olisa Metuh . <p> Another factor against speedy disposal of high-profile cases is the Constitutional presumption of innocence , which makes it extremely difficult to prove allegations of corruption in an adversarial system that @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ high-profile corrupt persons will remain a mirage . <p> The above scenario was responsible to the lack of speedy disposal of high-profile corruption cases . and fashioning out a speedy way to clear backlog of cases , among other measures . <p> A new rule of court procedure provides for the award of punitive cost by the court for frivolous litigation or delays and an inspectorate arm that ensures judges sit from 9:00a.m to 4:00p.m every working day . <p> In addition , judges require the notification and permission of the CJN to travel out of the country . <p> Judges of the lower courts are required to submit for assessment by the Federal Judicial Service Commission , quarterly report of cases handled , while higher courts submit their reports to the NJC . <p> In other to keep incompetent men and women out of the bench , appointment will be subject to written examination and interviews through rigorous screening and painstakingly appointment procedures . <p> To give effect to this anti-corruption stance , the NJC constituted the Corruption and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ by a retired Justice of the Supreme Court , Justice Suleiman Galadima , to serve as checks on the excesses of some bad eggs on the bench . <p> The committee has identified poor prosecution , absence of counsel for parties in court , reliance on irrelevant documentary evidence , multiplicity of charges , non-adherence to court rules/procedure , retirement/transfer of judges ; Kenneth was immediately arrested by the Police . <p> Also , in Ojoto , Anambra State , members of the Vigilante group arrested a vandal identified as Chinedu Ejikeme for vandalizing injection substation which is an NIPP project , located at Mmiri Ojoto area . In the course of interrogation , he confessed to be responsible for the vandalized 200KVA transformer , property of EEDC , located at Iruebenebe Community , Ojoto . <p> The Head , Communication of EEDC , Mr. Emeka Ezeh , said EEDC has gone a step further in apprehending the buyers of these vandalised items , because it is believed that that is the motivation the vandals have .
